topPRs.title: build: move all Go modules off op-geth onto upstream go-ethereum
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Moves every Go module in this repo off the op-geth fork, onto upstream go-ethereum and the current Optimism monorepo, and adds a CI check so op-geth can't come back.

All seven modules drop `replace github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum => github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth`: bailiff, op-conductor-mon, op-signer, op-txproxy, op-ufm, peer-mgmt-service and proxyd. One commit per module, then review follow-ups.

| | Version |
|---|---|
| `github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism` | `v1.21.0` |
| `github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum` | `v1.17.11-0.20261028021739-3dee18e7108c` |

- `v1.21.0` is the monorepo's tagged release of `2ad37990e12c`, on `develop` after the op-geth cutover (optimism#24176, then optimism#24350).
- The go-ethereum version is the one `v1.21.0` itself requires. go-ethereum has no release tag at or after that commit (the latest is `v1.17.10`), and Go's minimum version selection would pick this version anyway. infrastructure-services uses the same go-ethereum version.
- **Pion:** the patched `pion/stun/v3 v3.1.7` and `pion/dtls/v3 v3.1.5` now come in through the monorepo's own requires. peer-mgmt-service's `replace`s for them pinned older versions (v3.1.5 and v3.1.4), so they're dropped.

**What changed beyond the version bump**

- **Logging, all modules.** The monorepo's CLI log helpers moved to `op-service/log/logcli`, and `op-service/log` now has its own `Logger` type and its own global logger. Each module's logging moves from `go-ethereum/log` to `op-service/log`, which has the same functions and level constants.
- **proxyd: global logger.** After the cutover, `op-service/log`'s global logger discards records until `op-service/log.SetDefault` installs one. `SetLogLevel` used go-ethereum's `SetDefault`, so records that monorepo packages log through `op-service/log`'s global logger would have been dropped. It now uses `op-service/log.SetDefault`, which also installs the logger as go-ethereum's.
- **proxyd: interop access lists.** op-geth's `core/types/interoptypes` doesn't exist upstream. `checkInteropAndReturnAccessList` used only its `TxToInteropAccessList`, which is ported as `txToInteropAccessList`: the tx's CrossL2Inbox storage keys, raw and in order. Interop validation is unchanged: the strategies still parse, validate and deduplicate those raw entries, already through `op-core/interop/messages`.
- **op-txproxy.** `eth_sendRawTransactionConditional` used three op-geth-only things:
  - `types.TransactionConditional`, with its JSON codec, `Cost` and `Validate`. It's copied into `conditional.go` unchanged, with op-geth's unit tests.
  - The `params.TransactionConditional*` limits and error codes, copied with the same values (max cost 1000, -32003, -32005).
  - `rpc.JsonError`, replaced by `op-service/jsonrpc.Error`, which has the same fields and methods.

  The service's limits, error codes and wire format don't change. op-reth enforces a different limit (5000) and code (-32602), so op-txproxy stays stricter, as it was against op-geth.
- **op-conductor-mon.** op-conductor's API client now takes an op-service `client.RPC`. The geth RPC client is wrapped with `NewBaseRPCClient`, which caps every call at a timeout of its own, so the configured `rpc_timeout` is passed through. When `rpc_timeout` is unset, the wrapper's 10s default applies; before, the bare HTTP client had no limit.
- **bailiff in CI.** bailiff had no CircleCI jobs: it was missing from the path-filter mapping. It now gets lint and test jobs like the other modules, and this PR fixes what golangci-lint found on its first run (separate commit).
- **`no-op-geth` CI check.** `ops/scripts/check-no-op-geth.sh` fails when a tracked `go.mod` or `go.sum` names `ethereum-optimism/op-geth`, when a `go.mod` replaces `github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum` with anything (a fork, a local checkout), or when a `go.work` is committed. It can be run locally. The `no-op-geth` job runs it on every pipeline, so new modules are covered too. Ported from infrastructure-services#1785.

**Upstream go-ethereum traps checked**

Upstream go-ethereum can't decode OP deposit (`0x7E`) or post-exec (`0x7D`) transactions, so ethclient's block, receipt and tx reads can fail at runtime against L2 even though the code compiles. Checked every decode site:
- **proxyd:**
  - It decodes only user-submitted txs. A submitted deposit now fails decoding instead of being rejected later, so it's still rejected.
  - Its tx-monitor block fetcher reads only tx hashes from raw JSON.
  - Its flashblock decoder already skips txs it can't decode.
- **op-txproxy** decodes only submitted conditional txs. A deposit now fails decoding ("transaction type not supported") instead of failing the EntryPoint target check, so it's still rejected.
- **op-ufm** reads back only its own EIP-1559 txs and headers.
- No other module reads L2 blocks, txs or receipts through ethclient.

**Tests**

Per module, mirroring the CI `go-lint`/`go-test` jobs: `go mod tidy` (no diff), `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint fmt --diff` and `golangci-lint run` (v2.11.4), and `go test ./...` with `-checklinkname=0`. All seven pass. op-signer also builds with `CGO_ENABLED=0`.

- **proxyd:** new `TestTxToInteropAccessList` pins the ported helper: raw entries in order, across duplicate CrossL2Inbox tuples, other addresses ignored. The interop integration tests (`TestInteropValidation_*`, `TestTxFilter_*`) pass, including `StaticParseAccessPrevalidationCheck`: a malformed access list is rejected with -32602 and never reaches the filter, as on `main`.
- **op-txproxy:** op-geth's `TransactionConditional` tests are ported. A new marshal test pins the JSON forwarded to the backend; its expected strings were produced by op-geth's own type for the same values. New tests pin the cost limit (a cost of exactly 1000 passes, 1001 is rejected) and the error codes and messages, the latter also as a client receives them over JSON-RPC.
- **op-signer:** checked against `main` with a LOCAL-provider key over mTLS.
  - `eth_signTransaction` (EIP-1559) and `opsigner_signBlockPayloadV2` return byte-identical results from `main` and this branch.
  - The tx signature recovers to the key's address.
  - `op-signer --help` (flags and env vars) is identical.
  - The only difference is a trailing newline in the JSON-RPC response body (upstream's RPC server doesn't write one).
- **`check-no-op-geth.sh`:** passes on this branch. Against throwaway repos it fails, naming the file, for an op-geth `replace`, a local-path, versioned, block-form or quoted `replace` of go-ethereum, a root-level `go.mod`, op-geth in a `go.sum`, and a `go.work` at the root or in a module; it passes a plain go-ethereum `require`.
- **`govulncheck`** on every module reports no go-ethereum advisories. It still reports `gorilla/websocket` v1.5.3 (GO-2026-6278). That's already on `main` at the same version and pinned by the monorepo; its fix is only on an untagged commit, so it's left for a separate change.

**Additional context**

- op-txproxy reports go-ethereum's version as its app version (`cmd/main.go`), so its reported version changes from op-geth's to upstream's.
- CircleCI's path filter sends `.circleci/` changes to `run-all`, so this PR runs every module's jobs.

**Metadata**

- Fixes ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#385

topPRs.title: feat(proxyd): per-api-key alias configurable rate limits
topPRs.author: yashvardhan-kukreja
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds `[rate_limit.alias_overrides.<alias>]` so individual authenticated aliases can get their own rate limits on top of `use_auth_alias`.

- An alias that sets its own base (`base_rate` + `base_interval`, or `infinite_rate_limit = true`) uses only its own base and method overrides; global method overrides no longer apply to it.
- An alias with only `method_overrides` keeps the global base and global method overrides, replacing or adding individual methods.
- `infinite_rate_limit = true` on a per-alias method override leaves that method unlimited for the alias; `limit = 0` blocks it.

Invalid configs fail at startup: overrides without `use_auth_alias = true`, aliases missing from `[authentication]`, conflicting or incomplete fields, non-positive base rates or intervals, negative method limits, and empty overrides.

Also fixes the README sentence from #761 that still described method quotas as additional to the base.

Unchanged: IP-keyed limits, global `[rate_limit]` semantics, Origin/User-Agent exemptions, `global = true`, and the Redis key format.

**Tests**

- Unit tests for resolving the limits of each override shape, for validation (one row per error), and for choosing between override-alias, default-alias and IP limits.
- Integration tests for each override shape with memory and Redis, a shared quota across two instances on one Redis, and startup failures.

topPRs.title: feat(proxyd): consensus_out_of_range_wait for blocks just above consensus
topPRs.author: zhwrd
topPRs.body:
## Problem

In consensus mode, websocket subscriptions and HTTP requests see different heads:

- **WS:** `ProxyWS` connects the client to a single backend, so `newHeads` for block N fires as soon as that backend imports N.
- **HTTP:** `eth_getBlockByNumber(N)` is checked against the consensus latest block. That is the lowest head across the consensus group, refreshed every `consensus_poller_interval`, plus up to one HA heartbeat when `consensus_ha` is on. While N is above it, proxyd answers `null` itself (#552, #769), and state reads get `-32001`.

On a 1s-block chain, a client that fetches each block right after its `newHeads` notification loses this race on nearly every block. One example is Blockscout's realtime fetcher, which turns the `null` into `404 Not Found`, doesn't retry, and leaves the block to its catch-up indexer. We saw about one error per block and blocks reaching the explorer ~45s late.

## Change

New backend group option `consensus_out_of_range_wait`, default `0` (off). When set:

- A request that names a block above the consensus latest block, by at most `consensus_max_block_lag`, waits until consensus reaches that block or the wait elapses.
- It then goes through the normal rewrite path. Responses still come only from consensus backends, and a block that never reaches consensus is still answered as out of range.
- Backends are chosen after the wait. Consensus can advance during it by dropping a lagging backend, and that backend must not then serve the request.
- One HTTP request waits at most `consensus_out_of_range_wait` in total. That includes a batch, which is forwarded as several minibatches (`max_upstream_batch_size`, duplicate-ID groups). A request whose budget is already spent gets outcome `exhausted`. WS messages are forwarded once, so each may wait in full.
- Startup rejects a wait that is not shorter than the server timeout (`timeout_seconds`, default 10s).
- Blocks further ahead than `consensus_max_block_lag` can't be on any consensus backend yet, so they are answered immediately as today.
- CL consensus groups are unaffected.

Supporting changes:

- **Out-of-range error:** the rewrite error is now `*BlockOutOfRangeError{Block}`. It matches `ErrRewriteBlockOutOfRange` via `errors.Is`, so existing checks are unchanged.
- **Wait loop:** it rechecks the in-memory consensus state every 20ms and stops on timeout or when the client cancels.
- **Log ranges:** the block scan probes past the first out-of-range block, so a log range with both ends above the head waits for `toBlock`.
- **New counter:** `proxyd_group_consensus_out_of_range_waits_total{backend_group_name,outcome}` with outcomes `caught_up`, `timeout`, `too_far`, `canceled` and `exhausted`.

Waiting was chosen over routing the request to whichever backend is ahead for three reasons:

1. Consistency guarantees stay the same.
2. It covers every method the rewriter handles, `eth_getLogs`/`eth_newFilter` ranges included.
3. Routing ahead would need method-specific retry-on-missing logic and would still race the poller's per-backend head, which can be up to one poll interval old.

**Trade-offs:**
- A held HTTP request does not take a `max_concurrent_rpcs` slot, since that semaphore is only taken around the backend call. It does hold its connection and goroutine for up to the wait.
- Over WS, a held message keeps its `max_concurrent_ws_rpcs` slot.
- Server drain can take up to one wait longer.

**Not covered:** `eth_getBlockByHash` with the hash from `newHeads`, since proxyd can't place a hash relative to the head.

## Testing

- `integration_tests/consensus_out_of_range_wait_test.go` (new config `consensus_out_of_range_wait.toml`) covers:
  - the block is served once consensus advances mid-wait
  - `null` after the wait if consensus doesn't advance, without hitting the backend
  - no wait beyond `consensus_max_block_lag`
  - no delay for in-range requests
  - a batch whose elements are forwarded as separate minibatches (`max_upstream_batch_size = 1`) serves every element once consensus reaches its blocks
  - three minibatches spend one wait in total
- Unit tests for `highestOutOfRangeBlock`: it finds the max across methods and ranges (both ends of a log range above the head included) and leaves request params untouched.
- `TestStartRejectsOutOfRangeWaitAtServerTimeout` checks the startup check, with an explicit and with the default server timeout. Further unit tests cover `BlockOutOfRangeError` (`errors.Is`/`errors.As`).
- Not covered: a group of more than one backend in which consensus advances by dropping a lagging backend mid-wait.
- Test run: `go test ./...`, `go test -race` on the new test, and `golangci-lint run` (v2.11.4) all pass.

topPRs.title: proxyd: add opt-in rate limiting by authenticated alias
topPRs.author: bitwiseguy
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Addresses task 3 of this [RPC Hardening notion doc](https://app.notion.com/p/oplabs/RPC-Hardening-Work-Planning-3e6f153ee16280ea8fb8c3bc66ea4789).

Add opt-in `[rate_limit] use_auth_alias` so authenticated consumers sharing an egress IP get independent rate-limit buckets.

Base and method limits use the configured alias across HTTP requests, batch elements, and mapped WebSocket calls, with isolated buckets in memory and Redis. Unauthenticated requests retain IP-based limits. Default behavior and existing exemptions remain unchanged.

## Tests

New tests added that cover...

- Independent quotas for different aliases sharing an IP.
- Shared quotas across IPs and credentials using the same alias.
- Disabled-mode compatibility and alias/IP bucket isolation.
- Redis quota sharing across replicas.
- Batch rejection handling and HTTP/WS quota sharing.
- Rejection metrics attributed by alias.

The full proxyd test suite and focused race checks passed.

## Related Issues

* Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/core-team/issues/3251

topPRs.title: feat(proxyd): add flashblocks-aware routing
topPRs.author: paranoiacblack
topPRs.body:
**Description**

- Adds flashblocks-aware routing. When `eth_getBlockByNumber`, `eth_getTransactionCount`, `eth_getTransactionReceipt` and `eth_getBalance` are called with "pending" block numbers on chains producing Flashblocks, the request will be answered by a flashblocks-aware backend.
- Adds configuration that enables flashblocks-aware routing.
- Adds configuration that allows specifying exactly one flashblocks-aware backend group.
- Adds logic to parse JSON-RPC request's method and parameters to determine if it should be sent to the flashblocks-aware backend group or to normally configured backend group for the rpc method mapping. 

**Tests**

- Added tests for checking for pending JSON-RPC requests.
- Added integration tests for every request + param combination that can ask for information about the latest flashblock.
